ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Modeling and Verification of Embedded Systems. Prerequisites: Recommended but not essential CS 373, ECE 486 or equivalent, or consent of instructor. Students should understand basic concepts in logic and have some programming experience. Familiarity with automata theory will be useful. This course provides a rigorous introduction to modeling and verification techniques in the area of Embedded Systems. Particular emphasis will be placed on the real-time and distributed aspects of such systems. Topics covered include: formal models for real-time, distributed, and hybrid systems; model checking and deductive verification of invariance, safety, and stability properties; composition, abstraction, and hierarchical verification. Special attention is paid to software tools and engineering applications including real-time distributed systems, sensor networks, and autonomous vehicles. In the process we will encounter a large set of award winning papers and ideas.
